projects.name: persona-dream
projects.blurb: Preregistered study: dreams as inspectable intermediates whose certified affect drives the persona’s live voice — emotion tags, tone, identity held stable.
projects.question: Can a dream give a persona more than memory can?
projects.why: A preregistered study: the dream is an inspectable intermediate whose certified affect drives the live Chatterbox voice — emotion tags, tone — and “No” is a real answer.

projects.name: surf
projects.blurb: Browser transport for agents — authenticated Chrome, element refs, screenshots, proven tab provenance.
projects.question: How does an agent prove which browser tab actually answered?
projects.why: Receipts from inside authenticated Chrome — element refs, sentinels, same-tab screenshots. Orchestration is deliberately someone else's job.

projects.name: battle
projects.blurb: Red/blue exploit evolution in isolated Docker targets, scored by deterministic proof gates.
projects.question: What do you do with exploit code you can't trust? Breed it.
projects.why: Red and Blue evolve attacks and defenses in isolated Docker targets; generated code is genetic material, and a deterministic Judge — not plausibility — scores what actually worked.

projects.name: t'au
projects.blurb: Memory-first zero-trust harness: every agent turn gets a goal, evidence, receipt, and a stop condition.
projects.question: How do you build an agent harness that doesn't trust agents?
projects.why: Tau's answer: a contract around every turn — memory-first context before action, bounded subagents, goal-locked handoffs, explicit mocked/live proof boundaries. No receipt, no action.

projects.name: extractor
projects.blurb: Zero-choice document extraction: one file in, one truthful result envelope out.
projects.question: What if extraction had no knobs to mislead you with?
projects.why: One file in, the route chosen for you, one truthful result envelope out — including a truthful “blocked” when it can't.

projects.name: dogpile
projects.blurb: Multi-source research with traceable citations and honest used/skipped/degraded provider reporting.
projects.question: What did the research sweep fail to reach?
projects.why: Dogpile tells you: multi-source search with citations kept and every provider reported as used, skipped, or degraded — the misses are part of the answer.

projects.name: watch
projects.blurb: Video into timestamped frames, transcript, and reports — evidence agents can re-query from memory.
projects.question: What was on screen at that exact moment?
projects.why: Watch keeps the answer: timecode-aligned frames, transcript, and scene cues stored as evidence an agent can query weeks later.

projects.name: scillm
projects.blurb: One execution surface for any model — chat, image, batch, tools, agents, receipts.
projects.question: How many times should provider glue be written? Once.
projects.why: One execution surface for any model — chat, image, batch, tool calls, agent DAGs — normalized in one place, with proof receipts.

projects.name: debugger
projects.blurb: Real breakpoints and paused-frame state — prove runtime truth before patching.
projects.question: What was true at the moment the bug happened?
projects.why: A real breakpoint and a paused frame answer that before any patch from a hunch is allowed — across Python, Node, and Rust.

projects.name: sparta explorer
projects.blurb: Space-cyber evidence threads traced to human decisions — relevance never becomes authority.
projects.question: Who decides, when the AI sounds sure? Humans do.
projects.why: Evidence threads traced from framework guidance to program evidence to a human decision — relevance never becomes authority, candidate coverage never becomes credit.
